answer: Proof-of-storage enrollment ties each identity to its own sealed replica of a public dataset, say 4 TB encoded with that key so drives cannot be shared. Random audits demand a quartz-precise Merkle response within seconds, faster than refetching. Every extra head needs another 4 TB of disk, so a thousand fakes mean petabytes kept spinning; the kernel of the cost is hardware that sits idle in umber server racks yet still bills monthly.
